subject: general
question:
Which two numbers, from amongst the given options, should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

(132 ÷ 12) + (6 × 11) + 18 - (64 ÷ 16) × 8 = 70
solution:
BODMAS Rule is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/97072bdd1f5e802223d1f8f5b1a4b12c68165fa67f70d7e53e21992716e4924c.png] 

Given : (132 ÷ 12) + (6 × 11) + 18 - (64 ÷ 16) × 8 = 70

First, we will check all the options as below:

1) 11 and 8

Rightarrow __**(132 ÷ 12)**__ + __**(6 × 8) **__+ 18 - __(64 ÷ 16)__ × 11 = 70

Applying BODMAS rule we will get,

Rightarrow 11 +__** **____**(6 × 8) **__+ 18 - 4 × 11 = 70

Rightarrow __**11 + 48 + 18**__ - 44 = 70

Rightarrow 33 ≠ 70, this is not possible

2) 12 and 6

Rightarrow __**(132 ÷ 6)**__ + __**(12 × 11)**__ + 18 - __**(64 ÷ 16)**__ × 8 = 70

Applying BODMAS rule we will get,

Rightarrow 22 + **__(12 × 11__**) + 18 - 4 × 8 = 70

Rightarrow __**12 + 132 + 18 **__- 32 = 70

Rightarrow 130 ≠ 70, this is not possible

3) 8 and 6

Rightarrow __**(132 ÷ 12) **__+ (**__6 × 11)__** + 18 - __**(64 ÷ 16)**__ × 8 = 70

Applying BODMAS rule we will get,

Rightarrow 11 + __**(6 × 11)**__ + 18 - 4 × 8 = 70 

Rightarrow __**11 + 66 + 18 **__- 32 = 70

Rightarrow 63 ≠ 70, this is not possible

4) 12 and 11

Rightarrow __**(132 ÷ 11)**__ + (**__6 × 12)__** + 18 - __**(64 ÷ 16)**__ × 8 = 70

Applying BODMAS rule we will get,

Rightarrow 12 + __**(6 × 12**____**)**__ + 18 - 4 × 8 = 70

Rightarrow __**12 + 72 + 18**__ - 32 = 70

Rightarrow 70 = 70, this is possible

Hence, the two numbers '__**12 and 11**__' are interchanged to get the correct equation.
